messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGER — Unusual surge: /v1/auth/session session creations at 3.2k req/s, concentrated across a few proxy subnets. Potential session inflation attack.

Jordan: on it, paging SRE oncall. Seeing 3.2k req/s to auth endpoint, 98% from a handful of /24s via mobile proxies. Session creation latency up +80ms for users.

Maya (oncall): I got the page, taking lead. Can someone drop the hotspot metric link?

Jordan: https://dash.redwood.ai/metrics/alerts/1798612345 — shows spike between 15:08 and now. Also CPU on auth-service pods spiked to 95%.

Maya (oncall): Thanks. Quick triage — are these valid users failing auth or creating sessions repeatedly? Any 4xx/5xx pattern?

Jordan: 200 OKs dominating — looks like session inflation rather than brute-force credential failures. Large unique session ids generated, same device fingerprint series. UA and referrer look forged.

security-ops: tagging in — likely a session-flooding bot farm (amplifying free-tier registration). Recommend short-term fingerprint-based WAF + per-account velocity.

Maya (oncall): Agreed. Plan: 1) Apply targeted WAF rule to block UA/User-Agent regex and IP ranges (temporary). 2) Enforce per-account session-creation window: 3 sessions/min for free-tier. 3) Reduce free-tier burst_quota from 10 -> 3. 4) Disable /v1/bulk-import endpoint temporarily (possible amplifying vector).

Sam: I'll handle the gateway rule change. Patching API gateway now.

Sam: (code)
```
# gateway CLI
redwood-gw rule create --name session-fingerprint-block --match "ua_regex:/HijackedMobile/|fingerprint_hash:0x5a3f" --action block --ttl 30m
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for gateway-rule/session-fingerprint-block @sam
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded — rule id: gw-rule-1829

Sam: rule applied. Added quick IP deny for 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/25 via temporary ACL.

Sam: (command)
```
iptables -I REDWOOD_BLOCK -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j DROP
redis-cli -h acl-cache SADD blocked_ip 198.51.100.0/24
```

Maya (oncall): I'll push the rate-limit override in the auth service config. Patching configmap to introduce per-account window.

Maya (oncall): (config)
```
auth.rate_limits.free_tier.session_window = { \"per_min\": 3, \"burst\": 1 }
```

deploy-bot: configmap auth-config updated (v3.14.2) — rolling restart auth-service
authority-bot: auth-service pod roll started: auth-5, auth-6, auth-7

Jordan: Observability — session creation rate down ~65% within 4 minutes of rule. CPU trending down. Latency back to baseline for most users. Full dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/graphs/session-1798612345

support-anna: Support queue — I put a banner and notified top 10 affected customers via status page with a short note about \"temporary rate controls\". Raising a ticket for any customers who report legitimate blocked sessions.

Maya (oncall): Good. Question: do we want to fully disable /v1/bulk-import now or just 429 all requests?

security-ops: 429 is safer for short term to avoid data loss. We'll change to 429 with a header telling clients to backoff.

Sam: (command)
```
redwood-gw route update /v1/bulk-import --status 429 --response-header \"Retry-After: 60\"
```

deploy-bot: route update applied.

Maya (oncall): Next steps: keep WAF rule for 30m, monitor for false positives, keep per-account window for 2 hours, and run anomaly detection to fingerprint new clusters. If attack shifts, escalate to full IP blackhole.

security-ops: I've created a short-lived firewall rule to drop confirmed bot subnets; telemetry forwarded to sec-alerts channel. Also added fingerprint hash to shared blocklist.

Jordan: Noted minor false positive from one customer (mobile app v1.2.7). Support ticket #INC-2348 created; whitelist entry added for their account id: acct-8271.

Maya (oncall): Added temporary whitelist to ensure no business-critical customers impacted. Please attach any replay logs to the ticket.

support-anna: Ticket updated with logs from client and mitigation note. CS has flagged for manual review.

Maya (oncall): Preparing handoff to Sam in 30m. Will summarize in pager and drop follow-up runbook steps here.

Maya (oncall): RUNBOOK TL;DR — Identify fingerprint cluster -> apply WAF UA+fingerprint rule -> apply per-account session window (free-tier) -> reduce free-tier burst_quota -> 429 bulk-import -> monitor CPU/latency -> whitelist legitimate customers -> remove temporary rules after 2 hours if stable.

Sam: Copy — I'll take oncall at 16:15 UTC. Will keep rule in place until 18:15 unless metrics stable for 60m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — severity downgraded to P2. Alert quiet for 8m.

Maya (oncall): Closing loop: Good work. Postmortem owner: Jordan. Please include timeline, customer impact table, and suggested automation to detect session inflation earlier (e.g., unusual new-session-per-account delta > 50%/5m).

Jordan: Will do. Moving to follow-up doc and postmortem after handoff. Thanks :thumbsup:

Sam: taking it from here. I'll post updates in this thread if anything changes.
